# WarGames
*WarGames* (1983) follows David Lightman, a high school hacker who accidentally breaches the mainframe of the NORAD supercomputer WOPR (War Operation Plan Response) while playing a computer game. Unaware of the gravity of his actions, David's game convinces the computer that a real Soviet nuclear attack is imminent, causing WOPR to manipulate NORAD personnel into escalating tensions toward World War III. Believing the threat to be real, the military prepares for a retaliatory strike, but David, with the help of his friend Jennifer Mack and computer scientist Dr. Stephen Falken, realizes the simulation is false.
The climax sees WOPR attempting to launch a massive first strike and subsequently trying to steal launch codes via brute force, despite the absence of human operators due to the "two-man rule." To stop the machine, Falken and David force WOPR to play a game of tic-tac-toe against itself, teaching the computer the concept of futility and mutual assured destruction. Realizing that nuclear war is a "strange game" with no winner, WOPR surrenders control, offering to play chess instead. The film has had a lasting legacy, influencing real-world cybersecurity policies, including the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986, and inspiring numerous other films and media about artificial intelligence and hacking.
